messages:
maya: Kicking off preflight for the Cobalt customer private cluster (on-prem, air-gapped). Posting the checklist + known gotchas.

maya: TL;DR: need offline package bundle, BGP peering details from customer, IP plan + MTU, and GPU image bake. Target handoff Thurs 14:00 PT.

ajay: Thanks — can you attach the offline bundle spec? Also pinging @ops-jin for routing constraints.

maya: Uploaded spec here: internal:registry/cobalt/offline-bundle-v2.tar (customer will load via USB). Key bits pasted below:

maya: ```
- k8s v1.26 kubeadm assets (tar)
- containerd 1.7.1 rpm + offline snapshots
- nvcr.io GPU driver package (470.xx) + cudnn tar
- CRI hooks for device plugin v0.11
- seed-ca certs + k8s bootstrap token file
```

linus: Note on GPU drivers: the customer's Dell nodes need 470.161.x driver, we tested 470.161.03 in staging. Match exact minor version or kernel modules fail.

cory: For networking: customer will do BGP from their edge. We need: ASNs, peer IPs, prefix list, and whether they want us to advertise host routes or only services via MetalLB.

ops-jin: Asked infra vendor for MTU tests earlier — they saw fragmentation with 1500 -> need jumbo 9000 for RDMA on Mellanox. Customer said they can enable jumbos but requires downtime window.

maya: Adding to schedule: enable jumbo frames during maintenance window, validate RDMA by running ib_read_bw on two test nodes.

ajay: Any extra firewall rules? Customer firewall blocks egress to pypi/gcr — confirm our package mirror IPs and port 443 allowed.

maya: Right — customer must whitelist: registry.internal.cobalt:443 and ntp.pool.org:123. We'll provide exact IPs in the handoff doc.

linus: Bootstrapping notes for the team: use this kubeadm command on the first control plane node (airgapped):

linus: ```
kubeadm init --config /etc/kubeadm/cobalt-controlplane.yaml --upload-certs 
# then copy /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf to the operator laptop via USB
```

maya: Also: cluster CA will be pre-seeded. DO NOT run cert rotation during initial validate. We've had handoff failures when rotation ran before node join.

cory: Capacity planning: customer ordered 8 A10G GPUs (4 nodes x 2 GPUs). Our cost estimate shows baseline monthly GPU infra ~ $12k/mo for reserved capacity equivalent; mention this in the contract handoff.

ops-jin: Validation checklist I'll run post-join:
- control plane health (kubectl get cs)
- etcd snapshot and restore sanity check
- node GPU visibility (nvidia-smi inside device-plugin pod)
- RDMA throughput test (ib_read_bw)
- MTU/path-MTU test: iperf3 with --mtu flags
- kube-bench quick scan for CIS v1.6

maya: Example commands for GPU visibility:

maya: ```
kubectl -n kube-system get pods | grep nvidia
kubectl -n kube-system exec -it device-plugin-xxxxx -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv
```

ajay: One operational gotcha: swap must be off on all nodes. If the customer's imaging turned swap on, kubelet won't start. We'll add a preflight that checks /proc/swaps.

linus: Customer routing asks for host networks to be advertised. We prefer MetalLB in BGP mode to advertise service IPs only — avoids leaking pod IPs into customer fabric. Flagging for architecture decision in handoff.

cory: For rollbacks: keep a snapshot of the offline bundle and an annotated runbook on the USB. If driver install fails, we revert to previous kernel + driver using vendor recovery.

maya: I'll assemble the final handoff doc with the exact IPs, ASNs, image checksums, maintenance window, and runbook steps. Plan to share by Wed EOD for review.

ops-jin: I'll own post-handoff validation and the first-week burn-in checks. Will post results to this thread after each test.

sre-bot: Reminder: create an incident on-call rotation for the customer for the first 72h (automated schedule created).

maya: Thanks all — next sync Wed 09:00 PT to run through the commands and validate the offline bundle checksum.
